title: Houston ICE Shooting: Third Witness Victor Salgado Released; Grand Jury Moves Forward
excerpt: Victor Hugo Salgado Araujo — brother of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and an eyewitness to the July 7 Houston ICE shooting — was released from ICE detention after 54 days, following court orders freeing the other two witnesses. The Harris County DA announced plans to secure grand jury testimony from all three.
content:
On August 30, 2026, Victor Hugo Salgado Araujo — the brother of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and a passenger in the front seat during the fatal July 7 ICE shooting — was released from ICE custody at the Montgomery ICE Processing Center after being detained for 54 days following the shooting.

  • Victor was the third of three witnesses to be released; Daniel Tirado Pantoja and Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego had previously been ordered released by federal judges.
  • The government indicated it would likely approve Victor's application for a temporary legal status as a witness to a potential crime.
  • Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare announced that investigators had gathered essentially all physical evidence from the day of the shooting and were moving to secure sworn grand jury testimony from all three witnesses.

Federal records reviewed by Fox 26 revealed that ICE agents had mistaken Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's work van for one connected to their targets, and that ICE records attribute intelligence about a white van to the Texas DPS — an account DPS disputes. The Harris County DA confirmed that a substance found in the van was not a narcotic, contradicting a DHS characterization used to justify the stop.

The detention of the three eyewitnesses for weeks following the shooting drew widespread criticism from civil rights advocates who alleged the detentions were used to suppress testimony.
source: Houston Public Media / Texas Tribune / Fox 26 Houston
